title: Flow-Reserve Allocation & Scoped Eviction Playbook
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: As Redwood scales, we need a lightweight, repeatable protocol to allocate a floating pool of staff and cycle-level buffer (flow-reserve) that can be consumed by high-severity blockers or emergent customer requests without derailing committed OKRs. This ticket captures a playbook that standardizes when and how scope eviction (temporary or permanent) is triggered, how the float-pool is consumed, and the telemetry required to automate triage decisions.

Objectives:
- Define a 3-tier flow-reserve model (micro, standard, surge) with explicit trigger signals and governance.
- Create a scoped eviction matrix (temporary defer / de-scope / fast-track) so PMs and Eng leads can make consistent in-flight scope cuts.
- Codify float-pool staffing rules: who can be pulled, handoff expectations, and shadowing protocol.
- Integrate with capacity-simulator v2 and cycle dashboards so trade-offs can be modeled prior to approval.

Scope (what this ticket includes):
- Draft playbook doc with decision flowcharts and example scenarios.
- Templates for PM sign-off, engineering handover checklist, and on-call rotation for surge.
- Implementation plan for telemetry slices (blocked-days, burn-rate delta, customer-severity signal) in Console.
- Pilot run with two initiatives in Cycle 2026-W11 for validation.

Out of scope:
- Changes to payroll/comp models for staffing swaps.
- Long-term org changes to headcount allocation (this is an ops playbook, not a staffing policy).

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Conservative reserve sizing reduces rollout risk but increases chance of underutilizing float capacity; we recommend starting at a 5% micro + 10% standard reserve of committed FTEs and iterating based on pilot telemetry.
- Scoped eviction prioritizes user-impacting work; some visionary scope may be deferred which increases long-term roadmap risk — mitigate via clear re-onramp criteria.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Playbook doc published in Confluence with flowchart and three scenario examples.
- Two PMs and two Eng leads have signed the template and completed a tabletop exercise.
- Console dashboard shows the new telemetry slices and a sample simulated reserve consumption for at least one initiative.
- Pilot run retro with action items and updated playbook.

Risk & Mitigations:
- Risk: Teams may overuse reserve for low-priority tasks. Mitigation: require written PM justification and lead-engineer approval for each reserve pull; threshold automation for routine veto.
- Risk: Ambiguous skill matches when pulling from float pool. Mitigation: maintain a skills-indexed float roster and shadow pairing rules.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: Publish draft playbook and solicit design/eng feedback.
- Week 1: Implement telemetry slices (Console events).
- Week 2: Run two tabletop pilots and populate the float roster.
- Week 3: Execute live pilot on 2 initiatives and collect metrics.
- Week 4: Retro and ship finalized playbook.

- Capacity simulator scenario: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-cap-sim-v2-scenarios
- PR for dashboard slices: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1342
- Example tabletop notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-tabletop-notes-39217
